declaration_comparisons.name: QuantumBlockEncoding.GrayBasis.twist
declaration_comparisons.comparison: toFun and invFun both preserve q and conditionally flip b when q parity is nonzero. Since q mod2 is0 or1, this is exactly b xor(q mod2). Both inverse laws use the same parity case and flip involution.

declaration_comparisons.name: QuantumBlockEncoding.GrayBasis.equiv
declaration_comparisons.binder_audit: n TYPING; no existence, rank or nonzero-width premise
declaration_comparisons.comparison: Width0 is the inverse singleton LE encoding. Successor casts2^(n+1)=2^n*2, splits via finProdFinEquiv.symm into quotient and remainder, applies twist, recursively transforms q, swaps the pair and conses head/tail. Fin.consEquiv places the new bit at wire0 and previous coordinates at successors, exactly the source recursion and explicit inverse.
declaration_comparisons.proof_topology: Composition of explicitly invertible providers and recursive tail equivalence, not classical selection of a bijection

declaration_comparisons.name: QuantumBlockEncoding.GrayBasis.headBit
declaration_comparisons.binder_audit: index TYPING/input value; no finite-range condition
declaration_comparisons.comparison: Returns index mod2 when quotient parity is0, otherwise its binary flip. This equals the two-lowest-digits xor formula for every natural, without defining an off-range Gray register.
declaration_comparisons.proof_topology: Literal arithmetic formula with derived modulo bounds

declaration_comparisons.name: QuantumBlockEncoding.GrayBasis.equiv_head
declaration_comparisons.binder_audit: n,index TYPING; finite bound is in index type
declaration_comparisons.comparison: Literal definitional head identity, proved by rfl. No parity side condition or changed order.

declaration_comparisons.name: QuantumBlockEncoding.GrayBasis.equiv_tail
declaration_comparisons.binder_audit: n,index,wire TYPING; quotient legality derived from index.isLt and pow_succ, not an extra premise
declaration_comparisons.comparison: Definitional tail identity, proved by rfl, with a derived Fin-bound proof for the quotient. Coordinate shift is successor, not reversed-wire indexing.

declaration_comparisons.name: QuantumBlockEncoding.GrayBasis.headBit_even
declaration_comparisons.binder_audit: index input; even condition SOURCE; no width/range premise
declaration_comparisons.comparison: Proves unchanged quotient and new remainder1, then both quotient-parity cases. Exactly the source's head toggle for an even step, on all naturals.
declaration_comparisons.proof_topology: Even remainder transition plus parity cases

declaration_comparisons.name: QuantumBlockEncoding.GrayBasis.headBit_odd
declaration_comparisons.binder_audit: index input; odd condition SOURCE; no width/range premise
declaration_comparisons.comparison: Proves quotient increment and new remainder0; each parity branch proves the opposite next quotient parity. The xor changes cancel exactly as reconstructed before formal exposure.
declaration_comparisons.proof_topology: Odd remainder transition and quotient-parity toggle

declaration_comparisons.name: QuantumBlockEncoding.GrayBasis.adjacent
declaration_comparisons.signature: forall {n:Nat},first second:Fin(2^n),first.val+1=second.val -> exists target:Fin n,equiv n second=xBasisAction target(equiv n first)
declaration_comparisons.binder_audit: Implicit n and finite labels TYPING; next SOURCE; no nonzero-width, chosen-wire, oracle or gate premise
declaration_comparisons.comparison: Width0 derives contradiction from Fin1 bounds. Successor creates legal quotient labels from the finite bounds. Even first label gives equal tails and target0; odd first label gives adjacent tails, applies induction and shifts target to target.succ while preserving head. Equality of bit functions after Function.update means exactly one coordinate changes because no binary value equals its flip. It is existential, not a separately certified named-target algorithm or unique-existence declaration.
declaration_comparisons.proof_topology: Same width induction and both parity branches as preflight; no cyclic last-to-first extension
